newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia, Macedonia talk boosting trade - agency.
newsitem.headline: Croatia, Macedonia talk boosting trade - agency.

text.p: Croatian and Macedonian officials on Wednesday discussed liberalising and boosting mutual trade, which has shrunk from over $660 million a year since before the 1991-95 Balkan conflict, state news agency HINA reported.

It said the former constituent republics of ex-Yugoslavia prepared for concluding agreements on free trade and customs to follow accords on economic cooperation and promotion of mutual investments that were signed earlier.
The 1995 trade totalled a mere $106 million, of which Croatia exported $70 million worth of goods to Macedonia.
But since the two countries introduced new customs tariffs, it fell further to $69 million to the end of September this year, or 14 percent less than in the same period of 1995.
The fact that they have no direct payments system but use banks in third countries was seen by officials as a big obstacle, which had to be removed as a step to boosting trade.

To improve on poor results, they said companies had to increase their presence on the other country's market, and cited shipbuilding, electronic, construction and chemical industry, along with textiles and agriculture as fields with a good potential for stronger business cooperation. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
